_comment: The one list of user settings. Read by the engine (electron/settings.cjs) and by the CLI (crates/tweb-core/src/settings.rs) so the two cannot disagree on a name, a type or a default. `env` is the variable that already set this before the file existed; it still wins over the file. `applies` says when a change is picked up: live (within a second, no restart), new-tab, engine (next engine start), pane (next `tweb open`).

settings.description: Reverse the terminal wheel. Off follows the terminal, which already applies macOS natural scrolling.

On macOS, read the real pointer and trackpad (tweb-native-input) so a pane inside tmux gets pixel positions and precise, inertial scrolling instead of cells and wheel notches. Off uses the terminal's reports alone.
Page zoom a new tab starts at.
Highest frame rate a pane draws at. `tweb open --frame-rate` overrides it.
Drop to a low idle rate when nothing moves. `--no-adaptive-frame-rate` overrides it.
Let the terminal show through pages that paint no background. Electron engine only. `tweb open --transparent` turns it on for one pane.
Where downloads are saved. Empty means the system Downloads folder.
Width in cells of the box an IME composition is drawn in.
What a search typed in the omnibox (or a selection's "Search") opens: google, duckduckgo, bing, brave, kagi, ecosia, perplexity, or a URL with %s where the query goes.
Search suggestions in the omnibox: off, an engine name above, or a URL with %s returning OpenSearch JSON. Off by default because every keystroke typed there is sent to that provider.

Sites pinned to the Chrome engine (Okta Device Trust, Endpoint Verification, Cyberhaven). Each entry covers that host and its subdomains; the most specific entry across the three engine lists wins. A typed URL or a followed link to a pinned site opens it on that engine in the same tab; a redirect stays where it is and the engine badge offers the switch.
Sites pinned to the WebKit engine (macOS). Same rules as engine.chrome_sites.
Sites pinned to the Electron engine: an exception carved out of a broader chrome or webkit entry, or a site kept on Electron in a pane opened on another engine. Same rules as engine.chrome_sites.
